summary: Equity medians (geometric, nominal USD): US large cap 6.3% (n=7), US small cap 6.0% (n=6), global equity 6.8% (n=5), EM equity 8.1% (n=6), the last with a 3.0-8.8 range.
Bond medians: US cash 3.6% (n=6), US aggregate 4.6% (n=6), intermediate Treasuries 4.8% (n=7), IG corporate 5.2% (n=5), high yield 5.5% (n=7), EM USD sovereign 5.7% (n=8); IQRs 56-90bp.
Alternatives: private equity's 9.7% median (n=5) is the highest of any row; private credit 6.6% (n=4), hedge funds 5.6% (n=4), commodities 5.2% (n=7).

Widest disagreements, ranked by IQR (rows with at least four publishers): commodities 225bp (n=7), US small cap 188bp (n=6), private equity 155bp (n=5), private credit 143bp (n=4), EM equity 123bp (n=6).
This site's LTCMA differs most on UK equity (7.0% vs 9.0%, two publishers only), commodities (3.5% vs 5.2% median, n=7), gold (3.3% vs one publisher's 1.6%), US TIPS (4.5% vs 3.8%, n=4).
Prediction markets price zero Fed cuts in 2026 at 95.7% (Kalshi) and 95.8% (Polymarket); two cuts, flagged by Goldman Sachs AM, trade at 1.3% and 1.0%; UBS GWM CIO and Mercer expected easing.
Next FOMC: hold priced at 83.0% (Kalshi) and 82.5% (Polymarket), a 25bp hike at 16.5% on both, while BlackRock Investment Institute argues markets overprice Fed hikes.

US recession in 2026 priced at 3.5% (Kalshi) and 6.5% (Polymarket; contract terms differ), siding with the resilient-growth calls of Vanguard, Invesco and Mercer over Lazard's doubts on US resilience.

divergence_rule: public IQR >= 150bp with n >= 4, or >= 1 overweight and >= 1 underweight stance

divergences.label: US large cap
divergences.headline: US large cap: AI-driven earnings optimism versus valuation drag; seven estimates span 4.9-7.6 around a 6.3 median.

bull.argument: BNY Investments (7.6) assumes AI lifts earnings with valuations held flat; Fidelity International (6.4) counts on AI-aided revenue growth and payouts, net of a margin drag. Goldman Sachs AM and BlackRock Investment Institute, overweight, cite AI-driven earnings strength. T. Rowe Price (6.4) sits barely above the median, still citing rich valuations.
bull.data_used: Income, inflation and real-growth building blocks with an AI uplift to earnings; no valuation mean-reversion (BNY Investments); revenue growth, dividends, buybacks and margin normalization (Fidelity International).

bear.argument: Invesco (4.9) lets a steep multiple-compression drag offset real earnings growth and shareholder yield; Vanguard (5.1) says higher valuations cut returns; State Street (5.5) tempers its building blocks for valuation. PIMCO, underweight, sees almost no equity risk premium and a better bond Sharpe ratio; Lazard expects rotation away from US equities; Amundi is underweight.
bear.data_used: Starting multiples with assumed valuation mean-reversion, layered on dividend or shareholder yield, real earnings growth and inflation; equity risk premium versus bond yields (PIMCO).

divergences.what_to_watch: Whether AI-linked mega-cap earnings growth and margins hold up enough to sustain current multiples; P/E compression without matching earnings gains would support the lower-return camp.

divergences.label: US small cap
divergences.headline: US small cap: second-widest IQR of any row (188bp); valuation-anchored optimists versus rich-after-rally and weak-earnings views.

bull.argument: AQR (7.4) adds expected inflation to a valuation-based real return; BNY Investments (7.5) assumes a weak size premium as firms stay private longer, yet lands just under its broad-equity figure. T. Rowe Price (6.3, five-year horizon) upgraded the segment. Goldman Sachs AM, overweight, cites attractive valuations, expected Fed cuts, accelerating earnings and revived dealmaking.
bull.data_used: Valuation-based real return plus inflation (AQR); factor exposures and size premium (BNY Investments); valuation-anchored index forecast (T. Rowe Price); expected cuts, earnings momentum, M&A (Goldman Sachs AM).

bear.argument: Invesco (4.5, bottom of range) sees a smaller valuation drag than in large caps but weak long-run earnings growth, ranking small caps behind mid-caps; Vanguard (5.7) says the strong small-cap rally lifted valuations and cut expected returns much as for large caps; State Street (5.1) assumes higher volatility than for large caps.
bear.data_used: Starting valuations after the rally (Vanguard); long-run earnings growth and valuation drag in a building-block model (Invesco); volatility assumptions (State Street).

divergences.what_to_watch: Small-cap earnings versus Invesco's weak-growth assumption, and the Fed: Goldman Sachs AM leans on cuts; markets put zero cuts in 2026 at 95.7% (Kalshi) and 95.8% (Polymarket).

divergences.label: US high yield
divergences.headline: US high yield: carry and contained defaults versus near-record-tight spreads and an emerging default cycle.

bull.argument: Starting yield dominates: Invesco (6.1) nets credit losses and spread drag off a high average yield; BNY Investments (6.1) matches it while assuming spreads widen toward their long-run median; Fidelity International (5.9) keeps a modest premium over IG. Goldman Sachs AM, overweight, cites strong interest coverage, contained defaults, a better ratings mix and firm demand.
bull.data_used: Average yield minus expected credit losses; spread mean-reversion with defaults tied to spread (BNY Investments); interest coverage, ratings mix, defaults, M&A demand (Goldman Sachs AM).

bear.argument: Compensation is thin: Vanguard (5.2) calls credit valuations rich; State Street (4.6, bottom of range) finds only a modest premium over IG from spread term structure and default probabilities; AQR (5.0) sits below the median. PIMCO, underweight, reads near-record-tight spreads as complacent while defaults climb, and leans up in quality; Amundi is also underweight.
bear.data_used: Spread term structure and default probabilities (State Street); credit valuations (Vanguard); spreads versus historic tights and rising defaults (PIMCO).

divergences.what_to_watch: High-yield default rates and spreads: rising defaults with widening spreads would confirm PIMCO's default-cycle call; contained defaults let starting carry dominate, as the higher camp assumes.

divergences.label: Commodities
divergences.headline: Commodities: widest IQR of any row (225bp); AQR's futures premium versus State Street's roll-plus-collateral build; rationale often missing.

bull.argument: AQR (6.7, top of range) assumes equal-weighted futures keep earning a long-run excess return over cash, on top of a positive real cash return. Vanguard (5.7) reports a model output for a broad commodity index without commodity-specific commentary. Robeco (5.8, five-year horizon) ties outcomes to geopolitical conflicts and the dollar path.
bull.data_used: Long-run futures excess return over cash plus real cash yield (AQR); index-proxy model output (Vanguard); conflict and US dollar scenarios (Robeco).

bear.argument: State Street (3.2) builds returns from US inflation and dollar forecasts, a long-run roll return and collateral yield; Invesco (3.8) edged up on a firmer real-asset outlook and stresses diversifying return drivers; BNY Investments (2.3, bottom of range) expects low returns with high volatility, little changed, without explaining the drivers.
bear.data_used: Inflation, dollar, roll-return and collateral building blocks (State Street); real-asset outlook (Invesco); BNY Investments discloses no drivers.

divergences.what_to_watch: Realized roll yield and collateral returns versus the long-run futures premium AQR assumes, plus the dollar path that both State Street and Robeco flag.

divergences.label: Global govt bonds
divergences.headline: Global government bonds: PIMCO's high-conviction overweight versus BNY Investments' fiscal-strain underweight; estimates tightly clustered (IQR 23bp, n=3).

bull.argument: Higher starting yields have lifted expected returns: Robeco (5.3, top of range; USD-hedged, five-year horizon) makes that case while cautioning the gain is not costless. PIMCO, overweight with high conviction, sees desynchronized cycles and diverging central-bank paths creating country and curve opportunities, with global sovereigns adding income and diversification.
bull.data_used: Current sovereign yields hedged to USD (Robeco); cross-country divergence in business cycles and monetary policy (PIMCO).

bear.argument: BNY Investments, underweight, argues fiscal strain makes sovereign debt less attractive on a risk-adjusted basis and looks to real assets and private markets for diversification. Fidelity International sits here only on its number, just below the median (4.8 vs 4.9); its stance is overweight, citing income from higher curves and diversification in recessionary shocks.
bear.data_used: Fiscal strain and expected curve steepening (BNY Investments); current government yield curves as the income driver (Fidelity International).

divergences.what_to_watch: How sovereigns trade in the next growth scare: falling yields would support the diversification case; rising term premia on fiscal news would support BNY Investments' caution.

divergences.label: Private equity
divergences.headline: Private equity: illiquidity-premium optimists versus leverage-adjusted, net-of-fee models; estimates span 6.6-10.5 around a 9.7 median.

bull.argument: BNY Investments (10.5, top of range), overweight, layers a large illiquidity premium on public-equity factor exposure and expects private capital to finance AI innovation and infrastructure. T. Rowe Price, on a five-year horizon, makes private equity its highest forecast, citing the illiquidity premium and active management relative to public equity.
bull.data_used: Public-equity factor exposures plus an illiquidity premium (BNY Investments); Cambridge Associates global PE benchmark (T. Rowe Price).

bear.argument: AQR (6.6, bottom of range) models US buyouts as levered equity in a dividend discount model, net of fees; cheaper debt and more assumed multiple expansion lifted its estimate, yet it sees compressed private-asset premia versus positive real cash. State Street benchmarks historical private-equity returns to listed equities, adjusting for leverage and fees.
bear.data_used: Levered dividend-discount model with fee drag, debt cost and multiple assumptions (AQR); historical PE-versus-listed performance, leverage-adjusted and net of fees (State Street).

divergences.what_to_watch: Whether net-of-fee buyout returns keep a premium over listed equity after leverage adjustment, and the debt costs and exit multiples that drive AQR's model.

divergences.label: Private credit
divergences.headline: Private credit: income and illiquidity-premium case versus PIMCO's stress warnings and AQR's fee arithmetic; estimates span 5.0-9.2 (n=4).

bull.argument: T. Rowe Price (9.2, five-year horizon) cites an illiquidity premium and structural demand for private capital; Fidelity International (6.9) sees higher-rate income and no immediate stress. Goldman Sachs AM (higher yields than public credit, historically fewer defaults than syndicated loans), BlackRock Investment Institute (selected deals with lender protections) and Amundi are overweight.
bull.data_used: Cliffwater Direct Lending index (T. Rowe Price); floating-rate income at elevated policy rates; historical default rates versus syndicated loans; underwriting and lender protections.

bear.argument: AQR (5.0, bottom of range) models direct lending as levered floating-rate high yield whose fees absorb any illiquidity premium. State Street (6.4), just below the median, adds a senior-lending premium to public credit, net of fees. PIMCO, a high-conviction underweight outside asset-based finance, sees stress in middle-market direct lending and risk of poor recoveries.
bear.data_used: Public high-yield spreads, cash rates and fee drag in a levered model (AQR); senior-lending premium over public credit (State Street); PIK use, maturity extensions and recoveries (PIMCO).

divergences.what_to_watch: Middle-market default, PIK and recovery data, plus the cash-rate path behind floating-rate income: rising stress would back PIMCO; benign credit with high rates, the income camp.

regimes.cycle_phase: Resilient growth; inflation-focused central banks; higher-for-longer Fed; stretched valuations after Q2 risk rally
regimes.summary: Sharp Q2 rally in risk assets stretched equity valuations and lowered expected returns; sovereign yields stable, credit rich. No explicit risk tilt; valuations not deemed a basis for reallocating.

regimes.cycle_phase: No cycle call; valuation-based view after a third straight equity rally, with rich US equities and positive real cash rates.
regimes.summary: No market-timing call. Risk premia look compressed for equities and private assets relative to positive real cash and bond yields, and AQR expects lower equity excess returns.

regimes.cycle_phase: Resilient growth, moderating inflation, elevated yields; uncertain and possibly hawkish policy path
regimes.summary: Elevated valuations temper US equity returns; non-US developed markets look relatively better; higher yields lift bond expectations, narrowing the equity-bond gap and reinforcing fixed income diversification.

regimes.cycle_phase: Mid-cycle: rejuvenated expansion, less late-cycle than widely believed
regimes.summary: Base case Great Rewiring (50%): AI- and investment-led rejuvenated expansion with higher inflation, supportive for risk-taking; bull Luminous Renaissance 15%, bear Synaptic Decay 35%.

regimes.cycle_phase: Late cycle: resilient but downside-skewed growth, with a credit default cycle now beginning amid geopolitical rupture
regimes.summary: Geopolitical rupture, fragmentation, fiscal strain and an AI capex boom widen outcome tails; PIMCO favors resilience over reach via high-quality, globally diversified bonds and up-in-quality credit.

regimes.cycle_phase: Not explicitly stated; fragile growth and structural transition amid the Iran-war shock
regimes.summary: Beyond Iran headlines, Lazard sees structural shifts: a weaker dollar, improving non-US equity relative performance, and steeper developed-market curves, while US economic resilience looks increasingly doubtful.

regimes.cycle_phase: Mid-cycle; soft landing with policy easing
regimes.summary: Soft-landing base case: gradual Fed easing with possibly two cuts in 2026; credit mid-cycle; easing, AI capex and dealmaking are catalysts amid elevated valuations and fiscal risks.
risks: AI capex disappointment and market concentration

regimes.cycle_phase: Expansion: uneven growth entering 2026, improving through the year as confidence recovers, fiscal stimulus gains traction, tariff effects fade and the Fed eases.
regimes.summary: Constructive: supportive economic backdrop for stocks, AI capex and adoption driving gains, Fed easing toward 3.33%, weaker dollar; political noise seen as short-lived for markets.

regimes.cycle_phase: Structural paradigm shift from globalization to modern mercantilism, combined with an AI capex boom and resource grab
regimes.summary: Bridgewater sees a new regime shaped by national self-interest and AI investment. AI capex supports US growth, but inflation risks are structurally higher, and portfolios built for the old era are fragile.

regimes.cycle_phase: Steady expansion with broadly easing policy; growth, inflation and rates converging toward long-term averages
regimes.summary: Mercer expects steady 2026 global growth led by a resilient, AI- and fiscally-supported US, inflation near targets and easing policy, keeping overall market positioning broadly neutral.
risks: US policy uncertainty and Fed independence

regimes.cycle_phase: Growth re-accelerating into 2026 with fiscal and monetary support, as policy diverges across regions
regimes.summary: Moderately constructive long-run view: AI productivity lifts equity and private-market returns, while fiscal strain, steeper curves and a weaker dollar favor global diversification over sovereign duration.
risks: Weak demand for long-duration government bonds

regimes.cycle_phase: Stabilizing, more balanced but still uncertain phase after markets absorbed higher rates
regimes.summary: Markets have absorbed higher rates and activity has stabilized; valuations mostly normalized but elevated in US growth; returns stable to modestly lower, fixed income less forgiving.

regimes.cycle_phase: Not specified; long-term structural regime of geopolitical fragmentation and AI-driven growth with elevated inflation and volatility
regimes.summary: Fragmentation, high debt and tech/energy transitions keep macro volatility and inflation above pre-Covid norms; AI lifts long-run GDP growth, supporting equities while bonds stay attractive.

regimes.cycle_phase: Expansion with renewed Fed tightening: strong US growth and AI buildout, softer jobs data, and long yields at their highest since 2002.
regimes.summary: BII stays risk-on, overweighting US and EM equities on AI-driven earnings; sees markets overpricing Fed hikes, a dollar above fundamentals with limited upside, and structurally elevated long yields.
